484.h: Lens University is a private university. It was approved on 3 March 2025, when President Bola Tinubu granted operating licences to eleven new private universities, and its proprietors then received a provisional licence from the National Universities Commission so that teaching could begin. It was set up partly to meet the rising demand for university places, with an emphasis on combining theory with practical skills.
484.a: As a new university, Lens is still building up its academic structure, facilities and range of undergraduate programmes.
484.c: The university is on the Offa-Irra road at Ilemona, in Oyun local government area of Kwara State.

354.h: The Nigerian Defence Academy (NDA) is a military university that trains officer cadets for commissioning into the Nigerian Army, Navy and Air Force. It was established on 5 February 1964 as a reorganisation of the Nigerian Military Training College, itself the renamed Royal Military Forces Training College. It was modelled on India's National Defence Academy at Khadakwasla, and Indian Army officers helped run its early training, including its first commandant, Brigadier M. R. Varma. During the Nigerian Civil War of 1967 to 1970 it supplied officers for the armed forces' rapid expansion, and by the late 1970s its instructors were mostly Nigerian. The National Universities Commission records its status as a degree-awarding university from 1985.
354.a: Training at the NDA takes five years: four years of academic study leading to a degree and one year of military training.
354.c: The academy is based in Kaduna, Kaduna State.

505.h: Prince Abubakar Audu University (PAAU), formerly Kogi State University, is a public university owned by the Kogi State Government. It was established in 1999 under Governor Abubakar Audu, and in 2020 Governor Yahaya Bello renamed it in his honour. Its pioneer vice-chancellor was Professor S. K. Okwute, a chemist, who served from 2000 to 2005.
505.a: PAAU has eight faculties. Agriculture covers agricultural economics, crop and animal production, fisheries and aquaculture, soil and environmental management, food science and home science. Arts and Humanities includes history and international studies, English, theatre arts, Arabic, philosophy and Christian religious studies. Law teaches both common law and Islamic law. Social Sciences offers mass communication, economics, political science, sociology and geography, and Education pairs teacher training with science and religious subjects, library science and health education. The university also offers medicine, and its library provides e-library services.
505.c: It is located in Anyigba, Kogi State.

400.h: Edwin Clark University (ECU) is a private university founded by Chief Edwin Kiagbodo Clark, the elder statesman from Delta State, and owned by the Edwin Clark Foundation. First called Edwin Clark University of Technology, it was approved through the National Universities Commission on 11 May 2015 as Nigeria's 60th private university, and its first academic session began on 14 September 2015. Its founder had a long record in education: as Commissioner of Education in the former Mid-Western Region in 1968, he played a part in establishing the University of Benin.
400.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes and is licensed by the National Universities Commission.
400.c: It is located in Kiagbodo, the founder's home town in Delta State.

460.h: University on the Niger (UniNiger) is a private university owned by the Anglican Diocese on the Niger, based in Onitsha. The National Universities Commission approved it to begin teaching in the 2023/2024 session with 20 degree programmes. Its first matriculation, in 2024, was held at the CJ Patterson Auditorium of All Saints Cathedral, Onitsha. About 300 students were admitted, and the Obi of Onitsha, Igwe Alfred Achebe, attended and described the day as historic for Onitsha.
460.a: UniNiger started with 20 degree programmes across several faculties.
460.c: Its permanent site is at Umunya, in Oyi local government area of Anambra State.

507.h: Rivers State University (RSU) is a public university owned by the Rivers State Government. It began in 1972 as the College of Science and Technology and became a university around the end of the 1970s; Wikipedia gives 1980 and the National Universities Commission records 1979. It took the name Rivers State University of Science and Technology, and in March 2017 it was renamed Rivers State University.
507.a: RSU is the only university in Nigeria accredited to award degrees in marine engineering. Its Faculty of Sciences includes chemistry, biochemistry, physics, mathematics, computer science, animal and environmental biology, microbiology, plant science and biotechnology, geology and maritime science, alongside faculties of engineering, medicine, law, management and others, with more being added.
507.c: The main campus is in the Mile III area of Diobu, Port Harcourt.

445.h: Maduka University is a private university established in 2023. Its chancellor and founder is Samuel Maduka Onyishi. It received its licence from the National Universities Commission, began its first academic session in November 2023, and appeared in the Commission's bulletin of 6 May 2024 listing approved private universities. It matriculated 600 students for its first session.
445.a: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria has approved the university's schools of nursing, midwifery and post-basic nursing, with an admission quota, in addition to its other undergraduate programmes.
445.c: It is located at Ekwegbe, in Igbo-Etiti local government area of Enugu State, on the new Enugu-Nsukka road.

506.h: Olusegun Agagu University of Science and Technology (OAUSTECH), formerly Ondo State University of Science and Technology, is a public university owned by the Ondo State Government. It was established in 2008 under Governor Olusegun Agagu, after whom it is now named, and teaching began in January 2011.
506.a: The university focuses on science and technology programmes. Its library opened on 1 March 2011 at the mini-campus with about 850 books and moved to its present building on Igbokoda Road in 2017. A donation of 40,000 volumes in 2020, partly through the UK charity Books2Africa, helped grow the collection to nearly 48,000 volumes.
506.c: It is located in Okitipupa, in the riverine south of Ondo State.

394.h: Fountain University (FUO) is a private university founded on Islamic principles by the Nasrul-Lahi-L-Fatih Society of Nigeria (NASFAT). NASFAT began as a prayer fellowship for Muslim professionals. Its plan for a university came out of a strategic retreat at Akodo, Lagos, in 2000, and an academic summit in January 2004 produced an 18-member planning committee. The Federal Government granted the university its operating licence on 17 May 2007.
394.a: The university has five colleges, including the College of Basic Medical and Health Sciences, the College of Natural and Applied Sciences, and the College of Management and Social Sciences.
394.c: It is located in Osogbo, the capital of Osun State.
